## OP330 THE UBIQUITIN-LIKE PROTEIN UBIQUITIN D IS UP-REGULATED BY SYNERGY OF NOTCH AND PRO-INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES IN THE INFLAMED INTESTINAL EPITHELIA OF IBD PATIENTS
A. Kawamoto1, G. Ito2, T. Nakata2, S. Fujii2, K. Suzuki2, F. Ishibashi2, H. Shimizu2, S. Nagata2, S. Anzai2, R. Kuno2, K. Kuwabara2, M. Kawai2, J. Takahashi2, M. Hama2, K. Tsuchiya3, T. Nakamura2, R. Okamoto1, M. Watanabe1

1Gastroenterology And Hepatology, Tokyo Medical and Dental University, Tokyo/Japan

2Department Of Gastroenterology And Hepatology, Tokyo Medical and Dental University, Tokyo/Japan

3Tokyo Medical And Dental University, Tokyo/Japan

Contact E-mail Address:
akawgast@tmd.ac.jp

Introduction: It is well acknowledged that the intestinal epithelium of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients is exposed to pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and IFN-γ. We have previously shown that the Notch signalling pathway is also up-regulated in the intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) of such epithelia, and contributes to IEC proliferation and epithelial regeneration. The mechanisms and consequences of how these signals interact are little known.
Aims & Methods: We aimed to reproduce such an inflamed epithelial environment in vitro and explore the gene regulation involved. Microarray analysis was performed on a human colonic epithelial cell line LS174T where the Notch intracellular domain (NICD) was inducibly over-expressed by Doxycycline, while simultaneously adding TNF-α and IFN-γ. The expression of UBD was analysed by quantitative RT-PCR and western blot. The transcriptional activity of UBD was measured by a gene-specific promoter-driven luciferase assay. Human intestinal organoid lines were established from biopsies taken from the small intestine and colon of ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn’s disease (CD) patients undergoing screening endoscopy. Surgical tissues from the small intestine and colon of UC and CD patients were immunostained to compare the distribution of UBD expression in inflamed and uninflamed states.
Results: Microarray analysis revealed that out of the genes that were up-regulated by the simultaneous addition TNF-α and IFN-γ while NICD was over-expressed, the ubiquitin-like protein Ubiquitin D (UBD) which was observed to undergo a 597-fold increase was found to be the most up-regulated of them all. Quantitative RT-PCR and western blot confirmed a synergistically increased expression of UBD on simultaneous NICD over-expression with TNF-α and IFN-γ co-addition. UBD promoter-driven luciferase assay showed significantly increased promoter activity on simultaneous NICD over-expression and co-addition of TNF-α and IFN-γ in LS174T cells, revealing the expression of UBD to be regulated at the transcriptional level under this condition. Western blot of several human intestinal organoid lines derived from both the small intestine and colon of UC and CD patients showed increased expression of UBD on co-addition of TNF-α and IFN-γ, which was suppressed on addition of dibenzazipine, a Notch-signal inhibitor. Immunostaining of uninflamed small intestinal and colonic tissues from IBD patients showed UBD expression to be limited to crypt base columnar cells, whereas an increased number of UBD expressing IECs were seen in the inflamed small intestine and colon.
Conclusion: The Notch signalling pathway and the pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IFN-γ synergistically up-regulate the expression of UBD, possibly bearing crucial roles in protection and survival of IECs through the anti-apoptotic property of UBD.
Disclosure of Interest: All authors have declared no conflicts of interest.

## OP331 WNT5B UP-REGULATION IN THE MUCOSA OF PATIENTS WITH INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE COULD CONTRIBUTE TO THE REGENERATION OF INTESTINAL EPITHELIUM
I. Dotti1, E. Ferrer-Picón1, N. Planell2, E.H. Van Herk3, M. Cuatrecasas4, J. Panés5, A. Salas1

1Experimental Gastroenterology Laboratory, IDIBAPS, Barcelona/Spain

2Bioinformatics Platform, CIBERehd, Barcelona/Spain

3Academic Medical Center, Tytgat Institute for Liver and Intestinal Research, Amsterdam/Netherlands

4Department Of Pathology, Hospital Clínic, Barcelona/Spain

5Department Of Gastroenterology, Hospital Clínic, Barcelona/Spain

Contact E-mail Address:
idotti@clinic.ub.es

Introduction: Epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) has been postulated to contribute to wound healing1. Emerging evidence indicates that Wnt5b could play a role in EMT2. We hypothesize that Wnt5b is expressed in the intestinal mucosa of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and contributes to regeneration through EMT.
Aims & Methods: To test our hypothesis, we: 1) evaluated Wnt5b expression in the intestine of patients with IBD and 2) investigated the effect of Wnt5b on human epithelial organoid cultures (EpOCs)3. Human intestinal samples were used for in situ hybridization and RNAseq to characterize Wnt5b expression in controls and IBD patients. Intestinal crypts were used to generate EpOCs for subsequent incubation with Wnt5b, TGF-β or LY2157299 (TGF-βR1 inhibitor). Total RNA was isolated for transcriptional analysis. Migration assays were performed to check Wnt5b-induced mesenchymal changes in EpOCs.
Results:
WNT5B mRNA was expressed in both the lamina propria and the epithelium of healthy human gut. Its transcription was greater in inflamed, versus non-inflamed, IBD samples. In EpOCs, Wnt5b promoted changes resembling the TGF-β-induced phenotype. These included a significant up-regulation of EMT markers, TGF-β targets and TGF-β itself. Indeed, LY2157299 fully suppressed the Wnt5b-mediated changes. Finally, Wnt5b-treated EpOCs showed higher migratory potential compared to un-stimulated cultures.
Conclusion: In conclusion, we show that Wnt5b acts on intestinal epithelium by potentiating a TGF-β -dependent EMT response. Its up-regulation in IBD mucosa could promote epithelial cell migration, thus contributing to a regenerative response in the context of tissue injury.
Disclosure of Interest: All authors have declared no conflicts of interest.

1. Nieto MA, Huang RY, Jackson RA, Thiery JP. EMT: 2016. Cell 2016; 166: 21–45.
2. Harada T, Yamamoto H, Kishida S et al. Wnt5b-associated exosomes promote cancer cell migration and proliferation. Cancer Sci 2017; 108: 42–52.
3. Dotti I, Mora-Buch R, Ferrer-Picon E et al. Alterations in the epithelial stem cell compartment could contribute to permanent changes in the mucosa of patients with ulcerative colitis. Gut 2016.

## OP332 NOVEL HUMAN GUT XENOGRAFT MOUSE MODEL FOR INTESTINAL FISTULAS
R.S. Bruckner1, N. Marsiano2, E. Nissim-Eliraz2, E. Nir2, M. Leutenegger1, C. Gottier1, S. Lang1, M. R. Spalinger1, G. Rogler1, S. Yagel3, M. Scharl1, N. Y. Shpigel2

1Gastroenterology And Hepatology, University Hospital Zurich, Zurich/Switzerland

2Koret School Of Veterinary Medicine, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Rehovot/Israel

3Department Of Obstetrics & Gynecology, Hadassah University Hospital, Jerusalem/Israel

Contact E-mail Address:
ramona.bruckner@usz.ch

Introduction: Fistulas represent a frequent complication in Crohn’s disease (CD) patients and surgical resection is often required. Despite some progress in understanding the pathogenesis and improving the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), more effective medical treatments are required, especially for CD patients with fistula formation. Previously, we demonstrated that epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) plays a critical role for fistula development in CD patients. Preceding upregulation of TGF-beta, IL-13, TNF and their receptors along fistula tracts in CD patients seems to orchestrate a number of events contributing to fistula development by inducing EMT. Due to a lack of a reliable in vivo model, new drug developments are complicated. Here, we describe a new xenograft (XGR) mouse model of intestinal fistula resembling the human condition.
Aims & Methods: 12–18 weeks (w) old human fetal small intestine was transplanted subcutaneously onto the backs of SCID mice. After 12–16w, ∼15% of the mature xenografts spontaneously developed enterocutaneous fistulas. Using systemic LPS treatment followed by mild skin irritation adjacent to the transplant, we established a reproducible model system, resulting in enterocutaneous fistulas 2–4w later. Samples were analysed by immunohistochemistry staining (IHC) for EMT-, immune cell- and necroptosis markers, as well as RNA sequencing.
Results: Histopathological analysis of the fistulating XGR samples revealed a characteristic loss of villous structures and flattening of the intestinal epithelial cells lining the fistula tract, resembling transitional cells described in human CD fistula samples. IHC stainings for various EMT markers (e.g. SLUG, β6-integrin) showed similar expression pattern as in samples from fistulas of CD patients. The expression of the mesenchymal marker alpha-smooth muscle actin confirmed the hypothesis that EMT plays a critical role for the fistula development in the XGR samples, as well. Inflammation in the XGR was apparent up- and downstream to the fistulous tracts. Most of this inflammatory response consisted of human CD45+ cells, but only very few murine CD45+ cells. Further characterization revealed large numbers of human CD3+ cells. Collagen staining showed that those inflammatory regions were associated with extensive fibrosis suggesting extracellular matrix remodeling. We also detected strong staining for necroptotic markers (RIP kinases and MLKL) in the fistulated XGRs compared to unfistulated control samples. RNA sequencing of inflamed LPS-treated XGRs revealed a significant upregulation of genes related to IBD, necroptosis, ripoptosome and NF-κB signaling.
Conclusion: Our data demonstrate that the in vivo model recapitulates, both morphologically and mechanistically, the human disease. Necroptosis might be the underlying molecular mechanism driving inflammation, EMT and finally fistula formation in vivo.
Disclosure of Interest: All authors have declared no conflicts of interest.

## OP333 REPROGRAMMED ATOH1+ INTESTINAL EPITHELIAL CELLS CONTRIBUTE TO REGENERATE DAMAGED COLONIC MUCOSA IN DSS-INDUCED COLITIS
F. Ishibashi1, H. Shimizu1, A. Kawamoto1, G. Ito1, T. Nakata1, S. Fujii1, K. Suzuki1, R. Kuno1, S. Anzai1, K. Kuwabara1, M. Kawai1, J. Takahashi1, M. Hama1, S. Nagata1, K. Tsuchiya2, T. Nakamura1, R. Okamoto1, M. Watanabe1

1Department Of Gastroenterology And Hepatology, Tokyo Medical and Dental University, Tokyo/Japan

2Tokyo Medical And Dental University, Tokyo/Japan

Contact E-mail Address:
f.jazzmaster@gmail.com

Introduction: Atoh1 is a master transcription factor for secretory lineage cell fate commitment of intestinal epithelial cells (IECs). We have previously identified that Atoh1 expression is maintained throughout the differentiation process of secretory IECs, starting from early immature secretory progenitor IECs to terminally differentiated secretory-lineage IECs. Recent series of studies have demonstrated the plasticity of lineage-committed IECs, and their ability to be reprogrammed back to intestinal stem cells (ISCs) upon severe tissue injury. However, the comprehensive contribution of reprogrammed secretory lineage IECs in maintenance and regeneration of the intestinal mucosa remains unknown.
Aims & Methods: To identify the contribution of Atoh1+ secretory lineage IECs in homeostatic as well as colitic environment, we established an in vivo lineage tracing system. Mice carrying CrePGR knock-in allele at the Atoh1 gene locus was crossed with those carrying Cre-inducible reporter allele to generate Atoh1-reporter mice. Lineage tracing of Atoh1+ IECs was performed under homeostatic condition, and also under induction of dextran sodium sulphate (DSS) colitis. Immunohistochemical analysis was used to identify reprogramming of Atoh1+ IECs, as determined by the formation of Atoh1+ IEC-derived clonal ribbons (Atoh1+ICRs). Comprehensive gene expression of reprogrammed Atoh1+ IECs was examined by microarray. Reprogramming of Atoh1+ IECs was further analysed by In vitro assays using the 3D organoid culture technique.
Results: Under homeostatic condition, a certain number of Atoh1+ IECs were reprogrammed backwards to the IEC pool, as shown by the formation of Atoh1+ICRs. Interestingly, reprogramming events of Atoh1+IECs appeared to happen more frequently in the colon, compared to the small intestine. Those reprogrammed Atoh1+ IECs acquired gene expression profile comparable to genuine ISCs, as confirmed by microarray and GSEA analysis. Also, Atoh1+IEC-derived organoids, as well as de novo formation of Atoh1+ ICRs, could be established and confirmed in vitro. Such a formation of Atoh1+ICRs was significantly enhanced by DSS colitis-induced mucosal damage. Atoh1+ IEC-intrinsic gene expression analysis identified and featured substantial induction of NF-kB signalling by the colitic environment. Consistently, exposure to inflammatory cytokines and bacterial components appeared to enhance formation of Atoh1+ICRs in vitro, through activation of NF-kB.
Conclusion: Reprogrammed Atoh1+ IECs acquire ISC properties, and contribute to maintenance and regeneration of the colonic mucosa. Robust activation of the NF-kB pathway may play a key role in Atoh1+ IEC reprogramming under the colitic environment.
Disclosure of Interest: All authors have declared no conflicts of interest.

## OP334 THE ROLE OF PH-SENSING RECEPTOR TDAG8 (GPR65) IN INTESTINAL INFLAMMATION
I. Tcymbarevich1, J. Cosin Roger1, S.M. Richards2, K. Baebler1, M. R. Spalinger1, G. Russo3, K. Atrott1, I. Frey-Wagner1, C.A. Wagner4, B. Misselwitz1, K. Seuwen2, G. Rogler1, C. De Vallière1

1Gastroenterology And Hepatology, University Hospital Zurich, University of Zurich, Zurich/Switzerland

2Novartis Institutes for Biomedical Research, Basel, Switzerland, Basel/Switzerland

3Functional Genomics Center Zurich, ETH Zurich/University of Zurich, Zürich/Switzerland

4Institute of Physiology, University of Zürich, Zürich/Switzerland

Contact E-mail Address:
Jesus.Cosin@uv.es

Introduction: The two major forms of inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), typically result in decrease of extracellular pH of the affected mucosa. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) identified over 240 non-overlapping single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNP) associated with IBD. G-protein-coupled receptor 65 (GPR65) or T-cell death associated gene 8 (TDAG8) has been reported to be a genetic risk factor for IBD in recent GWAS. TDAG8 belongs to a family of proton-sensing GPCRs, including TDAG8, ovarian cancer G-protein coupled receptor 1 (OGR1) and GPR4. However, the role of TDAG8 is not fully understood.
Aims & Methods: In this study we investigate the role of TDAG8 in a murine IBD model. Chronic colitis was induced in WT and Tdag8−/− (KO) mice with 4 cycles of 2% DSS in drinking water for 7 days followed by 10 days of regular drinking water. Colon specimens were obtained and RT-qPCR and immunohistochemistry (IHC) were perfomed. Quinescent peritoneal macrophages (MΦs) from WT and Tdag8−/− mice were isolated, cells were treated for 24 h with pH 6.8 serum free medium to activate TDAG8, using pH 7.6 as negative controls. RNA was isolated for RNA sequencing.
Results: In the chronic colitis model, no significant differences in the typical inflammatory markers were observed between WT and KO groups. However, mRNA expression of IFNγ, TNF, IL6, iNOS was increased in the KO group, but no significant differences of IL17a, Gata3, Foxp3 and RORc were detected. IHC staining revealed that DSS-treated Tdag8−/− mice showed increased immunoreactivity of MΦ marker F4/80 compared to WT and water controls. Protein staining of T cell marker CD3 showed no difference between WT and Tdag8−/− mice. Interestingly, mRNA and protein expression of OGR1 were downregulated in Tdag8−/− colon tissue. To further examine the role of TDAG8 in MΦs, we performed RNA-sequencing upon a 24 h pH shift from pH 7.6 to pH 6.8. Pathways in mouse MΦs, mediated by TDAG8, were positively enriched for regulation of lymphocyte and leukocyte activation, apoptosis and M1 regulation. Conversely, pathways in TDAG8-deficient MΦs were upregulated for cytokine production involved in inflammatory response and M2 regulation. Moreover, expression of OGR1 was significantly downregulated in TDAG8−/− MΦs.
Conclusion: No significant differences for colitis activity were observed in chronic DSS colitis in WT and Tdag8−/− mice, suggesting that TDAG8-dependent anti-inflammatory responses are not able to down-regulate inflammation in this IBD model. Although lack of TDAG8 did not affect outcomes in the murine chronic colitis model, TDAG8 was able to reduce the inflammatory response of macrophages. TDAG8 also upregulates expression of the pro-inflammatory pH receptor OGR1, potentially providing a feedback loop for pH dependent immune activation.
Disclosure of Interest: All authors have declared no conflicts of interest.

## OP335 PRO-INFLAMMATORY HUMAN CD11C+ MACROPHAGES, BUT NOT THEIR TOLEROGENIC CD11CDIM OR CD11C− COUNTERPARTS, ARE EXPANDED IN THE INFLAMED MUCOSA FROM PATIENTS WITH INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE
D. Bernardo1, I. Mora-Gutierrez1, A. C. Marín1, A. Montalban-Arques1, S. Fernandez-Tome1, A. Diaz-Guerra1, R. Caminero-Fernandez2, S. Casabona2, P. Miranda2, F. Casals2, M. Caldas Álvarez2, M. Jimenez2, F. De La Morena2, C. Santander1, M. Chaparro1, J. P. Gisbert1

1Instituto Investigación Sanitaria Princesa (IIS-IP) & CIBEREHD, Madrid/Spain

2Department Of Gastroenterology, Hospital Universitario de La Princesa, Madrid/Spain

Contact E-mail Address:
d.bernardo.ordiz@gmail.com

Introduction: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), is a chronic inflammation of the human gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Macrophages (MΦ), the most abundant GI-mononuclear phagocytes, are critical at shaping immune responses since they typically maintain the mechanisms of immune tolerance in health, although they can also exacerbate immune responses during inflammation. However, despite their relevance modulating GI-immune responses, there is not much information about their properties in the human GI-tract.
Aims & Methods: Our aim was to characterize human GI-MΦ subsets, phenotype and function both in health and in IBD patients. To that end, human intestinal biopsies were obtained from healthy controls and IBD patients (including UC and CD; both active and quiescent). Tissue was disaggregated and the lamina propria mononuclear cells characterized by flow cytometry. In other cases, intestinal biopsies were cultured overnight to obtain GI-secretomes which were used to assess the mucosa capacity to recruit circulating CD14+ monocytes (enriched from the blood from healthy controls) on transwell culture assays.
Results: Human intestinal MΦ (identified within singlet viable cells as CD45+HLA-DR+CD14+CD64+) were further divided into CD11chigh, CD11cdim and CD11c− subsets. While the CD11chigh subset resembled the phenotype of circulating phagocytic (Dextranhigh) pro-inflammatory CD14+ monocytes (CX3CR1+, SIRPαhigh, CCR2+, CD40+), the CD11cdim subset displayed an intermediate phenotype towards the CD11c− MΦ subset, which was not phagocytic (Dextranlow), had higher expression of HLA-DR and CD64 and lower expression of CX3CR1, SIRPα, CCR2 and CD40. CD11c+ MΦ displayed a higher production of IL-1β both in resting conditions and after LPS stimulation, compared with the CD11c− subset, which produced larger amounts of IL-10 and was hyporesponsive to LPS stimulation. In health, CD11chigh MΦ were the predominant subset in the distal GI-compartments (distal and proximal colon) while CD11c− MΦ were in a higher proportion in the terminal ileum and became predominant in the duodenum. Total MΦ numbers were increased in the inflamed colon from IBD patients (both UC and CD), although not on the non-inflamed tissue from the same patients or from quiescent patients, due to specifically higher numbers of the CD11chighsubset. Finally, colonic secretomes from healthy controls recruited circulating CD14+ monocytes, while such capacity was further increased on those from inflamed IBD patients (both UC and CD) but not on quiescent patients.
Conclusion: MΦ subsets are likely to represent transition stages from newly arrived pro-inflammatory monocytes (CD11chigh) into transient (CD11cdim) and resident (CD11c−) MΦ as reflected by the mucosal capacity to recruit circulating CD14+ monocytes, which was indeed further increased on active IBD patients where the CD11chigh macrophages are expanded.
Disclosure of Interest: All authors have declared no conflicts of interest.

## CAN COLONIC POLYPS BE DIAGNOSED IN REAL TIME? - ROOM E3____________________

## OP336 DOES CHROMOENDOSCOPY REDUCE COLORECTAL NEOPLASIA DURING SURVEILLANCE IN LYNCH SYNDROME? A RANDOMIZED TRIAL
J. Haanstra1, E. Dekker2, A. Cats3, F.M. Nagengast4, J. Hardwick5, S. Vanhoutvin3, W. De Vos Tot Nederveen Cappel6, H. Vasen7, J. Kleibeuker1, J.J. Koornstra1

1Gastroenterology And Hepatology, University Medical Center Groningen, University of Groningen, Groningen/Netherlands

2Gastroenterology And Hepatology, Academic Medical Center, Amsterdam/Netherlands

3Gastroenterology And Hepatology, The Netherlands Cancer Institute-Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Hospital (NKI-AVL), Amsterdam/Netherlands

4Gastroenteroly And Hepatology, Radboud University Medical Centre, Nijmegen/Netherlands

5Gastroenterology And Hepatology, Leiden University Medical Center, Leiden/Netherlands

6Isala Clinics, Zwolle/Netherlands

7Gastroenterology And Hepatology, The Netherlands Foundation for the Detection of Hereditary Tumours, Leiden/Netherlands

Contact E-mail Address:
j.f.haanstra@isala.nl

Introduction: Lynch syndrome (LS) is associated with an increased risk of colorectal carcinoma (CRC). Regular surveillance at 1–2 yearly intervals has shown to reduce this risk. Still, LS patients develop CRC, frequently in the proximal colon. Chromoendoscopy is reported to be superior to white-light endoscopy in LS with respect to the detection of flat adenomas. The aim of this study was to determine whether chromoendoscopy reduces colorectal neoplasia at follow-up endoscopy.
Aims & Methods: In a prospective randomized controlled multicenter trial 246 proven mismatch repair gene mutation carriers (mean age: 46 years, range 21–70 years) were randomized between conventional white-light colonoscopy and colonoscopy using chromoendoscopy in the colon proximal from the splenic flexure. After 2 years, both groups underwent colonoscopy using chromoendoscopy. The number of neoplastic lesions at baseline and at follow-up colonoscopy was recorded.
Results: The number of patients with neoplasia in the entire colon was not significantly different between chromoendoscopy and white-light colonoscopy (36/118 (0 CRC) versus 33/123 (2 CRC), p = 0.28). Using chromoendoscopy, significantly more proximal adenomas were detected compared with conventional white-light colonoscopy during the first procedure (44 versus 26 adenomas, p = 0.04). Chromoendoscopy took significantly more procedure time than conventional colonoscopy (p < 0.01), due to a significant difference in median withdrawal time (18 versus 12 minutes, p < 0.01). At follow-up colonoscopy after 2 years, no difference was found with respect to the number of patients with neoplastic lesions in the entire colon between the groups (35/118 (4 CRC) versus 29/118 (1 CRC), p = 0.56). The number of proximal adenomas found was also not significantly different (36 versus 47, p = 0.22).
Conclusion: Chromoendoscopy increases the detection of adenomas in LS, but does not significantly reduce the adenoma detection rate at follow-up endoscopy.
Disclosure of Interest: All authors have declared no conflicts of interest.

## OP338 A STUDY ON DIAGNOSTIC ABILITY TO DISTINGUISH BETWEEN ADENOMAS AND INVASIVE COLORECTAL CANCERS USING COMPUTER-AIDED ENDOCYTOSCOPY
K. Takeda1, S. Kudo1, Y. Mori1, M. Misawa1, S. Kataoka1, Y. Maeda1, Y. Ogawa1, K. Ichimasa1, T. Kudo1, K. Wakamura1, T. Baba1, E. Hidaka1, F. Ishida1, H. Inoue2, M. Oda3, K. Mori3

3Graduate School Of Informatics, Nagoya University, Nagoya/Japan

Contact E-mail Address:
ktluck1208@yahoo.co.jp

Introduction: Endocytoscopy (EC) enables in vivo observation of nuclei at about 500-fold magnification during gastrointestinal endoscopy[1]. We have reported the usefulness of EC for colorectal lesions, but in clinical practice it seemed that there is a need for an easy-to-use diagnostic aid system for trainees with little experience. To address this task, we have developed a computer-aided diagnosis system for EC imaging (EC-CAD) that provides fully-automated classification of colorectal lesions (2, 3). And we have recently reported its diagnosing ability for invasive colorectal cancer[4]. Whether it is a lesion at risk of lymph node metastasis is important in considering the indication of surgical operation. Therefore, it is very important to distinguish lesions that may have lymph node metastasis such as invasive cancers from other lesions. In this task, it is thought that the EC-CAD can be a very useful diagnostic tool.
Aims & Methods: The aim of the present study was to evaluate diagnostic ability to distinguish between adenoma and invasive colorectal cancer. EC-CAD analyzes EC images based on the information from nuclei and texture analysis. All 296 features (eight features from nuclei, 288 from texture analysis) are used as the data for evaluating EC images and EC-CAD automatically present the pathological diagnosis. We used a support vector machine (SVM) to help classify these many features. EC-CAD requires machine learning for construction of diagnostic algorithm. We used 8761 EC images for machine learning in the process of construction of the model. And we selected randomly 200 EC images, which were different from images used for machine learning, from data base of EC images for test data. In addition to the predicted pathological diagnosis, EC-CAD simultaneously present the probability of diagnosis calculated by SVM. When the diagnosis probability was 90% or more, the sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, PPV, NPV were 90.9%, 100%, 95.9%, 100% and 93.1%, respectively.
Conclusion: This study indicates the usefulness of EC-CAD system for to distinguish invasive colorectal cancer from adenoma. In considering surgical indication for colorectal lesions, it was suggested that the high diagnostic ability for invasive colorectal cancer of the EC-CAD may be useful for determining treatment strategies.

## OP339 ENDOSCOPIC AND MOLECULAR CHARACTERISTICS IN COLORECTAL SERRATED LESIONS REPRESENT SUBCLASSES OF THE SERRATED NEOPLASIA PATHWAY
H. Aoki1, E. Yamamoto2, H. Yamano2, H. Matsushita3, K. Yoshikawa3, R. Takagi3, E. Harada3, Y. Tanaka3, T. Harada4, T. Sugai5, H. Suzuki1

1Dept. Of Molecular Biology, Sapporo Medical University, Sapporo/Japan

2Department Of Gastroenterology And Hepatology, Sapporo Medical University, Sapporo/Japan

3Department of Gastroenterology, Akita Red Cross Hospital, Akita/Japan

4Center for Gastroenterology, Teine-Keijinkai Hospital, Sapporo/Japan

5Department of Molecular Diagnostic Pathology, Iwate Medical University, Morioka/Japan

Contact E-mail Address:
hironori_a1123@yahoo.co.jp

Introduction: Colorectal serrated lesions (SLs) include hyperplastic polyp (HP), traditional serrated adenoma (TSA) and sessile serrated adenoma/polyp (SSA/P). SLs are important premalignant lesions, but its clinical and biological features are not fully understood.
Aims & Methods: To establish accurate colonoscopic diagnosis and treatment of SLs, we aimed to clarify the associations between morphological, pathological and molecular characteristics in SLs. A total of 401 premalignant and malignant colorectal lesions were enrolled in this study. Microsurface structures were assessed by magnifying colonoscopy according to Kudo’s pit pattern classification system. Type II pit pattern was subcategorized into classical Type-II, Type II-Open (Type II-O) and Type II-Long (Type II-L). Biopsy specimens were obtained from all lesions for genomic DNA extraction, after which lesions were treated by endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) or endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD). BRAF/KRAS mutations and methylation of CpG islands were analyzed by pyrosequencing. CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP) status (CIMP-high, -low and -negative) was determined by using the five markers (MINT1, −2, −12, −31 and p16).
Results: Pit patterns of the 401 colorectal lesions were as follows: Type II (n = 48), Type II-L (n = 15), Type II-O (n = 91), Type II plus III/IV (n = 23), Type II-L plus III/IV (n = 28), Type II-O plus III/IV (n = 36), Type II-L plus V (n = 4), Type II-O plus V (n = 9) and Type III/IV (n = 147). Type II-O was tightly associated with sessile serrated adenoma/polyps (SSA/Ps) with BRAF mutation and CIMP-high. Majority of lesions with simple Type II or Type II-L were hyperplastic polyps (HPs), while mixtures of Type II or Type II-L plus III/IV were characteristic to traditional serrated adenomas (TSAs) (sensitivity, 69%; specificity, 95%). Type II-positive TSAs frequently exhibited BRAF mutation and CIMP-low, while Type II-L-positive TSAs were tightly associated with KRAS mutation and CIMP-low. Analysis in lesions containing both premalignant and cancer components suggested that Type II-L-positive TSAs may develop to KRAS mutated/CIMP-low cancers, while Type II-O-positive SSA/Ps develop to BRAF mutated/CIMP-high cancers.
Conclusion: Our results suggest that Type II subtypes may reflect distinct molecular subclasses in the serrated neoplasia pathway, and that they could be useful hallmarks to identify SLs at a high risk to develop CRC.

K. Suzuki, S. Kudo, T. Kudo, Y. Mori, K. Wakamura, M. Misawa, Y. Ogawa, Y. Maeda, K. Takeda, H. Nakamura, T. Hayashi, T. Baba, F. Ishida

Contact E-mail Address:
kenichi.suzuki.19860617@gmail.com

Introduction: Endocytoscopy (EC) is a next-generation endoscopy that enables diagnostic imaging at 450× magnification. To date, excellent results have been achieved using EC classifications for qualitative diagnosis and assessment of depth of invasion of colorectal lesions (neoplasia/non-neoplasia accuracy: 96.5%; accuracy for carcinomas with massive submucosal invasion (SM-m): 96.3%). (1, 2)
Aims & Methods: In the EC classifications, lesions diagnosed as EC3a vary extensively from adenoma to SM-m, including some lesions that are unsuitable for endoscopic treatment. ## OP341 COMPUTER-AIDED DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEM USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR PREDICTING THE NBI INTERNATIONAL COLORECTAL ENDOSCOPIC CLASSIFICATION OF COLORECTAL TUMORS
J. Byeon1, E.M. Song1, S.H. Lee2, K.J. Change2, S.W. Hwang1, S.H. Park1, D. Yang1, B.D. Ye2, S. Myung1, S. Yang1, B.H. Park2, N.K. Kim2, J.B. Seo2

2Asan Medical Center, Seoul/Korea, Republic of

Contact E-mail Address:
jsbyeon@amc.seoul.kr

Introduction: Image enhanced endoscopy such as narrow-band imaging (NBI) can help endoscopists predict the histopathology of colon polyps through various NBI finding classification systems such as the NBI international colorectal endoscopic (NICE) classification. However, the accurate diagnosis by the NBI system requires a significant learning curve. We developed a computer-aided diagnostic system using artificial intelligence and investigated its usefulness to predict the NICE classification of colorectal tumors.
Aims & Methods: An experienced, board-certified gastrointestinal endoscopist classified the NICE classification of NBI near-focus images of 133 endoscopically resected colorectal tumors from 98 patients (25 tumors classified as NICE type I; 89 as NICE type II; 19 as NICE type III). Of these, 106 images were used as a training image set with which the computer-aided automated diagnostic system was developed and trained. Deep learning method based on the convolutional neural network and weakly supervised learning method with visualization of class activation map were used to develop the diagnostic system. The other 27 NBI images were used as a test image set.
Results: The computer-aided automated diagnostic system yielded an overall diagnostic accuracy of 84.4% for the test image set. In the analysis using the test set, the specific diagnostic accuracy was 88.7% for the NICE type I lesions (sensitivity, 64.0%; specificity, 94.3%), 84.4% for the NICE type II lesions (sensitivity, 91.1%; specificity 71.1%) and 95.7% for the NICE type III lesions (sensitivity, 80.0%; specificity, 98.5%). As for the NICE type I polyps suggesting hyperplastic polyps, the negative predictive value was 98.1%. The class activation map suggested that the computer-aided diagnostic system might see the representative portion of tumor surface which is typical for each NICE type.
Conclusion: The computer-aided diagnostic system using artificial intelligence was useful to predict the NICE classification of colorectal tumors. Further investigations will be needed to improve the accuracy and to apply the system in real-time colonoscopy.

## OP342 LONG-TERM PROTON PUMP INHIBITOR USE INCREASES INTESTINAL DYSBIOSIS, GUT PERMEABILITY, INFLAMMATION AND MORTALITY IN PATIENTS WITH LIVER CIRRHOSIS
A. Horvath1, F. Rainer2, M. Bashir3, B. Leber1, B. Schmerboeck1, H. Grønbæk4, H.J. Møller5, T. Madl6, A. Groselj-Strele7, P. Fickert2, P. Stiegler1, V. Stadlbauer2

1Department Of Transplantation Surgery, Medical University of Graz, Graz/Austria

2Department Of Gastroenterology And Hepatology, Medical University of Graz, Graz/Austria

3Department For Endocrinology And Diabetology, Medical University of Graz, Graz/Austria

4Department Of Hepatology And Gastroenterology, Aarhus University Hospital, Aarhus/Denmark

5Department Of Clinical Biochemistry, Aarhus University Hospital, Aarhus/Denmark

6Institute Of Molecular Biology And Biochemistry, Medical University of Graz, Graz/Austria

7Core Facility Computational Bioanalytics, Medical University of Graz, Graz/Austria

Contact E-mail Address:
angela.horvath@medunigraz.at

Introduction: Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use is highly common in patients with liver cirrhosis, often without proven indication, although recent studies demonstrated an association between their use and the mortality risk in this cohort. The underlying mechanisms however are not fully understood.
Aims & Methods: In this study, we suggest a link between long-term PPI use, intestinal dysbiosis, increased gut permeability, and inflammation leading to increased mortality. We analysed the intestinal microbiome composition of 87 cirrhotic patients with and without ongoing PPI therapy based on sequencing data of the hypervariable region 1–2 of the 16S rRNA gene in order to identify biomarkers for PPI-associated intestinal dysbiosis. Gut permeability as assessed by lactulose-mannitol ratio, sucrose recovery, diamine oxidase and zonulin levels in stool, intestinal (calprotectin in stool) as well as hepatic inflammation (sCD163 and sMR) were analysed at inclusion. Outcome data regarding complications of cirrhosis and mortality were collected for an average of 37 months.
Results: The use of PPI was associated with significant oralisation of the gut microbiome composition. The most pronounced difference between PPI users and non-users was the high Veillonella parvula abundance which was closely associated with an increased abundance of Streptococcus salivarius and Streptococcus parasanguinis. Dysbiosis was accompanied by an increased gut permeability (increased lactulose-mannitol ratio, sucrose recovery and zonulin in stool), intestinal (elevated calprotectin levels in stool) and hepatic inflammation (increased levels of macrophage activation markers, sCD163 and sMR). Higher V. parvula abundance was also associated with a higher risk to develop complications of liver cirrhosis, including severe infections, as well as with higher mortality.
Conclusion: Our data show that in cirrhotic patients with long-term PPI therapy, the intestine is increasingly colonized by bacteria coming from the oral cavity. This is associated with increased gut permeability, intestinal inflammation, risk for portal decompensation and mortality. The indication for PPI therapy in cirrhotic patients should therefore be carefully evaluated.

## OP343 CO-ADMINISTRATION OF PROBIOTIC WITH OMEGA-3 FATTY ACIDS IN NAFLD MANAGEMENT: EVIDENCE FROM ANIMALS TO RANDOMIZED CLINICAL STUDIES
N. Kobyliak1, T. Falalyeyeva2, G. Mykhalchyshyn1, O. Dynnyk3, D. Kyriienko4, I. Komisarenko1

1Endocrinology, Bogomolets National Medical University, Kyiv/Ukraine

2Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, Kyiv/Ukraine

3Bogomolets Institute of physiology of the Ukrainian National Academy of Sciences, Kyiv/Ukraine

4Kyiv City Clinical Endocrinology Center, Kyiv/Ukraine

Contact E-mail Address:
nazariikobyliak@gmail.com

Introduction: We have previously shown that in rats with momosodiume glutamate induced obesity supplementation of alive probiotics mixture with omega-3 leads to more pronounced reduction for steatosis degree (0.73 ± 0.11 vs 0.93 ± 0.22, p = 0.199) which accompanied with significant decreasing of triglyceride (5.1 ± 0.25 vs 6.26 ± 0.23, p < 0.05) accumulation in liver as compared to probiotic alone. Despite of animal data, randomized placebo-controlled trials (RCT) in NAFLD are still lacking in humans.
Aims & Methods: In respect to our experimental data we studied, in double-blind single center RCT, the efficacy of co-administration of probiotic with omega-3 vs. placebo in type 2 diabetes patient with NAFLD detected on ultrasonography (US). A total of 48 patients met the criteria for inclusion. They were randomly assigned to receive “Symbiter Omega” combination of probiotic biomass supplemented with flax and wheat germ oil (250 mg of each, concentration of omega-3 fatty acids 1–5%) or placebo for 8-weeks administered as a sachet formulation in double-blind treatment. The primary main outcomes were the change in fatty liver index (FLI) and liver stiffness (LS) measured by Shear Wave Elastography (SWE). FLI a validated prediction score for hepatic steatosis severity designed Bedogni et al. Secondary outcomes were the changes in transaminases activity, serum lipids and cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, INF-γ) levels. ANCOVA was used to assess the difference between groups.
Results: All subjects completed the study and received more than 90% of prescribed sachets. Both probiotic and placebo were well tolerated and during study period the participants reported only several minor adverse events. In probiotic group FLI significantly decreased from 83.53 ± 2.60 to 76.26 ± 2.96 (p < 0.001) and but remained static in the placebo group (82.86 ± 2.45 to 81.09 ± 2.84; p = 0.156). In respect to our other primary endpoint the changes of LS measured by SWE in both interventional groups were insignificant, but more pronounced decrease was observed for interventional group as compared to placebo. Analysis of secondary outcomes showed that co-administration of probiotic with omega-3 lead to significant slight body weight loss, reduction of waist circumference, level of serum gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase (GGT), triglycerides (TG) and total cholesterol (TC). Conclusion: In this RCT, we confirmed animal data previously reported by us, that co-administration of probiotic with omega-3 can reduce liver fat, improve serum lipids, metabolic profile and reduce chronic systemic inflammatory state. Therefore, modulation of the gut microbiota with probiotic and different nutraceuticals represents a new branch in NAFLD management, but further studies in larger cohorts are required to determine this beneficial effect.

## OP344 ORAL ALGINATE SOLUTION REDUCES SENSITIVITY TO ESOPHAGEAL ACID PERFUSION IN PATIENTS WITH HEARTBURN. INTERIM REPORT OF A DOUBLE-BLIND, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED STUDY
J.L.S. Ooi1, P. Woodland1, D. Sifrim2

1Wingate Institute For Neurogastroenterology, Barts and the London School of Medicine, Queen Mary University, London/United Kingdom

2Wingate Institute, Queen Mary University London Wingate Institute Centre for Digestive Diseases, London/United Kingdom

Contact E-mail Address:
joanne.ooi@gmail.com

Introduction: Oral alginates are well known to reduce symptoms from gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD) by reducing/modifying reflux episodes forming a raft capping gastric contents and the postprandial acid pocket. In vitro studies in our lab demonstrated a protectant effect of alginates on human oesophageal mucosa lasting at least 60 min. We hypothesised that a second mechanism of action of alginates, i.e. topical mucosal protection, may contribute to reduction of symptoms in GORD patients.
Aims & Methods: To evaluate the effect of oral alginate on heartburn perception induced by intra-oesophageal acid perfusion. 21 adults with endoscopy-negative heartburn underwent 2 study visits, 2 weeks apart in a double-blind crossover study. 10 ml alginate (Gaviscon Advance, Reckitt Benckiser, Hull, UK) or placebo was given 15 minutes prior to oesophageal acid perfusion. Acid perfusion (10 minutes HCL pH 1, at 10 ml/min) was performed 10 cm above the manometrically identified lower oesophageal sphincter with subjects sat upright. Subjects reported time to first perception of heartburn (latency), and symptom intensity at the end of acid challenge on a scale of 0 (no heartburn) to 10 (maximum heartburn). Patients underwent impedance-pH reflux monitoring “off PPI” for accurate phenotyping.
Results: Compared to placebo, alginate pre-treatment produced increase in latency and decrease in intensity of acid-induced heartburn. When all 21 subjects were analysed, latency to heartburn increased from 60 (34–107) seconds with placebo to 90 (47–190) seconds with alginate, (p = 0.0524). When only the 12 patients with pathological acid exposure were analysed (AET 8.3% (5.6–12.9) (true NERD) the effect on latency was more pronounced (from 54 (34–80) second with placebo to 199 (58–190) seconds with alginates (p = 0.04). The intensity of heartburn perception was significantly reduced by alginate pre-treatment compared to placebo. The intensity score went from 0.69 (0.52–0.87) with placebo to 0.54 (0.30–0.80) with alginate (p = 0.029).
Conclusion: Oral alginate appears to reduce sensitivity to acid perfusion in patients with heartburn, particularly more so in those patients with increased acid exposure (true NERD). This effect might add to the reduction in reflux events. Studies are ongoing to confirm this preliminary results in a larger group of patients, and to uncover the mechanisms underlying the mucosal protectant effect of alginates in vivo.

## OP345 SYMPTOM ASSOCIATION PROBABILITY DETERMINES THE OUTCOME OF BACLOFEN THERAPY IN REFRACTORY GASTRO-OESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE
A. Pauwels, E. Deloose, V. Boecxstaens, C. Broers, T. Vanuytsel, J. Tack

Targid, Katholieke Universiteit Leuven, Leuven/Belgium

Contact E-mail Address:
ans.pauwels@med.kuleuven.be

Introduction: A significant proportion of patients with gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD) remains symptomatic while on proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy. PPIs significantly reduce the proportion of acid reflux, however they have no effect on non-acid reflux which can provoke symptoms in GORD patients. Baclofen, a γ-aminobutyric acid agonist, is able to decrease both acid and non-acid reflux. To date, studies with baclofen focused on mechanistic aspects in patients with proven ongoing weakly acidic reflux, but the symptomatic outcome of patients with refractory GORD symptoms has not received much attention.
Aims & Methods: The aim of this study was to assess the efficacy of baclofen 10 mg t.i.d. vs placebo as add-on therapy in GORD patients with insufficient response to PPI therapy, in a randomized, parallel, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Patients with an incomplete control of typical GORD symptoms (heartburn/regurgitation) in spite of PPI therapy were randomized into add-on baclofen 10 mg or placebo t.i.d. for 4 weeks to b.i.d. PPIs. Prior to the study and at the end of the treatment, patients underwent a 24 h impedance-pH monitoring. All patients were asked to fill out the ReQuest diaries starting 2 weeks prior to inclusion and continued during the entire course of the study. Data of the diaries were averaged per week. Reflux parameters post-treatment were compared to baseline using Wilcoxon signed rank test and were compared between baclofen and placebo using Mann-Whitney test. The differences in different ReQuest domains were compared using mixed models.
Results: 60 patients were included (age 47.5y (range 19–73), 41f/19 m), with 31 patients into the baclofen arm and 29 into the placebo arm. One patient decided not to start with the medication and 5 patients did not complete the study due to side effects (headache, nausea, drowsiness); all 5 of them were taking baclofen at that time. Final analyses was performed on 26 patients in the baclofen arm and 28 patients in the placebo arm. There was a decrease in total nr. of reflux episodes (p = 0.0019), the nr. of non-acid reflux episodes (p = 0.048) and the nr. of reflux episodes with a high proximal extent (p = 0.0057) in the baclofen condition compared to baseline, while no differences were observed in the placebo condition. When dividing patients into symptom association probability (SAP)- (n = 29) and SAP+ (n = 25) at baseline, we found a significant time by condition by SAP interaction for general wellbeing (p = 0.0091), with a significant difference in SAP+ patients between placebo and baclofen (p = 0.0434, after correction). There was no difference between placebo and baclofen condition at the end of the treatment period in SAP-patients. At baseline, women had a lower general wellbeing compared to men (p = 0.0044). Men tended to feel worse after placebo, while women improved both under baclofen as well as placebo (time by condition by gender interaction p = 0.0881). The presence of increased reflux parameters at baseline did not predict the outcome of baclofen add-on treatment.
Conclusion: This study confirms that baclofen decreases different reflux parameters in PPI refractory patients. We showed that only the SAP+ patients show general wellbeing benefit from treatment with baclofen. Women appear to be more sensitive to a placebo effect.
Disclosure of Interest: All authors have declared no conflicts of interest.

## OP346 GASTRO-ESOPHAGEAL REFLUX AFTER PERORAL ENDOSCOPIC MYOTOMY AS COMPARED WITH HELLER’S MYOTOMY: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW WITH META-ANALYSIS
A. Repici1, L. Fuccio2, R. Maselli3, F. Mazza3, L. Correale3, D. Mandolesi2, C. Bellisario3, A. Sethi4, M. Kashab5, T. Rösch6, C. Hassan7

1Dept. Of Gastroenterology, Ist. Clinico Humanitas Rozzano Dept. of Gastroenterology, Milano/Italy

2Deprtment Of Medical And Surgical Sciences, S.Orsola-Malpighi University Hospital, Bologna/Italy

3Digestive Endoscopy Unit, Division Of Gastroenterology, Humanitas Research Hospital, Rozzano, Milan, Italy, Rozzano/Italy

4Gastroenterology, Columbia University, New York/United States of America/MD

5Johns Hopkins Medicine, Baltimore/United States of America

6Klinik Für Interdisziplinäre Endoskopie, Clinic for Interdisciplinary Endoscopy, Hamburg/Germany

7Gastroenterology, Nuovo Regina Margherita Hospital, italy/Italy

Contact E-mail Address:
alessandro.repici@humanitas.it

Introduction: Per-Oral Endoscopic Myotomy (POEM) represents a less invasive alternative, as compared with conventional laparoscopic Heller’s myotomy (LHM), for achalasia patients. It cannot be excluded, however, that the lack of fundoplication in the POEM procedure may result in a higher incidence of reflux disease, as compared with LHM.
Aims & Methods: Aim of our meta-analysis was to systematically assess the incidence of reflux disease after POEM and LHM, when taking into consideration symptoms, endoscopic and pH-monitoring findings. This systematic review was carried out in according with the guidelines of the preferred reported items for systematic review and meta-analyses. Literature search with PubMed, EMBASE, SCOPUS, Google Scholar and the Cochrane Central Register of Clinical Trials was performed to identify full articles on the incidence of gastro-esophageal reflux symptoms, endoscopic- and pH-monitoring-findings following POEM and LHM (with fundoplication). Heterogeneity among studies was assessed by using the I2 statistic, and explored by means of sensitivity, subgroup and meta-regression analyses.
Results: From a total of 296 and 1379 records, 19 and 28 prospective studies, including 1542 and 2581 subjects who underwent POEM and LHM, respectively, were included. Pooled rate of post-procedure symptoms was 19.5% (95% CIs: 16.3–23.1; I2:43.3%) after POEM, and 8.8% (95% CIs: 5.3%−14.1, I2:80%) after LHM, respectively. Pooled rate estimate of abnormal acid exposure at pH-monitoring was 39.0% (95% CI, 24.5%–55.8%; I2:85%) after POEM, and 16.8% (95% CI, 10.2%–26.4%, I2:86%) after LHM, respectively. Rate of post-POEM esophagitis (grade A to D, Los Angel Classification) was 29.4% (95% CI: 18.5–43.3%, I2: 93%) after POEM, and 7.6% (95% CI: 4.1; 13.7%, I2: 62.5%) after LHM. At meta-regression, heterogeneity was partly explained by POEM approach and study population.
Conclusion: Incidence of reflux-disease appears to be significantly more frequent after POEM than after LHM with fundoplication. pH-monitoring and appropriate treatment after POEM should be considered in order to prevent long-term reflux-related complications.

## OP347 ESSENTIAL ROLE OF INTERLEUIKIN-33-INDUCED INNATE LYMPHOID CELLS IN DEVELOPMENT OF EOSINOPHILIC ESOPHAGITIS IN MICE
N. Oshima, S. Ishihara, H. Sonoyama, N. Yamashita, N. Fukuba, Y. Mishima, I. Moriyama, K. Kawashima, N. Ishimura, Y. Kinoshita

Gastroenterology And Hepatology, Shimane University School of Medicine, Izumo/Japan

Contact E-mail Address:
n-oshima@med.shimane-u.ac.jp

Introduction: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the esophagus characterized by mucosal infiltration of eosinophils. Although enhanced mucosal T helper type 2 (Th2) cell cytokine response is associated with the pathogenesis of EoE, the details are not fully understood. Interleukin (IL)-33 is a member of the IL-1 cytokine family that is constitutively expressed in epithelial cells. Epithelial-derived IL-33 induces innate lymphoid cell group 2 (ILC2) activities in various organs, which subsequently activates Th2 cytokines and leads to development of eosinophil-related allergic diseases. However, little is known regarding the roles of IL-33 and ILC2 activity induced by it in the pathogenesis of EoE. In the present study, several experimental protocols were designed to clarify these issues.
Aims & Methods: Using intraperitoneal sensitization with ovalbumin (OVA) followed by intranasal challenge with OVA in 8-week-old BALC/c mice, an EoE model was established. The presence of eosinophil infiltration-related esophagitis was confirmed by histological findings, while esophageal expressions of IL-33, IL-5, and IL-13 were examined by real-time PCR. Furthermore, production of IL-33 by cultured epithelial cells (Het1A) was examined by flow cytometry (FACS). To further investigate the effect of IL-33 on the pathogenesis of EoE, we established another model using 8-week-old BALB/c mice with intraperitoneal injection of recombinant IL-33 (control, PBS injection). IL-33-induced esophageal infiltration of eosinophils (Siglec F+ and CD11b+) and ILC2 cells (Lineage−, CD25+ and CD127+) was detected by FACS. In addition, the expression profiles of Th2- and allergy-related genes in esophageal tissues were investigated in this model using a PCR array system.
Results: In the OVA-induced EoE model, expressions of the IL-33, IL-5, and IL-13 genes in esophageal tissues were increased. In association with those cytokine levels, esophageal mucosa showed marked infiltration by eosinophils. Production of IL-33 by esophageal epithelial cells (Het1A) was clearly confirmed by FACS. In the IL-33-injected model, we found esophageal mucosa thickening following infiltration of eosinophils as well as the presence of other various inflammatory cells. Also, PCR array analysis demonstrated that injection of IL-33 significantly induced expressions of a variety of Th2- and allergy-related cytokines in the esophagus as compared to control mice. Moreover, FACS results clearly showed esophageal infiltration by CD25+ and CD127+ ILC2 cells, which was closely associated with the expression profiles of Th2- and allergy-related cytokines.
Conclusion: IL-33-induced ILC2 cell activity leads to infiltration of esophageal mucosa by eosinophils via production of Th2- and allergy-related cytokines, which may play an important role in EoE development.
Disclosure of Interest: All authors have declared no conflicts of interest.

A. Straumann1, A. J. Lucendo Villarin2, S. Miehlke3, M. Vieth4, C. Schlag5, U. Von Arnim6, J. Molina-Infante7, D. Hartmann8, A.J. Bredenoord9, C. Ciriza De Los Rios10, S. Schubert11, S. Brueckner12, A. Madisch13, J. Hayat14, J. Tack15, A. Schoepfer16, R. Greinwald17, R. Mueller17, S. Attwood18

Introduction: Eosinophilic Oesophagitis (EoE) is a rapidly emerging, chronic-inflammatory disease of the oesophagus. Until now, no approved drug therapy is available, although swallowed topical corticosteroids have indicated efficacy in the treatment of EoE.
Aims & Methods: To evaluate in a pivotal Phase 3 trial efficacy and safety of a novel budesonide orodispersible tablet formulation specifically designed for EoE for the induction of clinico-histological remission in adult patients with active EoE. Eighty-eight patients were randomised to receive 6-weeks double-blind (DB) treatment with either 1 mg budesonide orodispersible tablets (BUL 1mg) twice daily (BID) (n = 59) or placebo BID (n = 29). Non-responder could receive further 6-week open-label induction (OLI) treatment with BUL 1 mg BID. Primary endpoint: Rate of clinico-histological remission. Results: BUL 1 mg BID was highly statistically superior to placebo in achieving remission/improvement in clinical, endoscopic and histological endpoints (see table). A prolonged treatment of up to 12-weeks increased the overall cumulative clinico-pathological remission rate up to 84.7%. In 3 patients (5.1%) under BUL 1 mg BID vs none under placebo, suspected local fungal infections with endoscopic and clinical signs (all mild) were histologically confirmed by sensitive Grocott staining. ## OP349 LONG-TERM TREATMENT OF EOSINOPHILIC OESOPHAGITIS WITH SWALLOWED TOPICAL CORTICOSTEROIDS: DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF A THERAPEUTIC CONCEPT
T. Greuter1, C. Bussmann2, E. Safroneeva3, A. Schoepfer4, L. Biedermann1, S. Vavricka1, A. Straumann5

1Gastroenterologie Und Hepatologie, University Hospital Zurich, Zürich/Switzerland

2Division Of Pathology, Histopathology Viollier, Basel/Switzerland

3Inst. Für Sozial- Und, Universität Bern ISPM, Bern/Switzerland

4Dept. Of Gastroenterology & Hepatology, University Hospital Lausanne (CHUV), Lausanne/Switzerland

5Gastroenterology Fmh, Swiss EoE Research Network, Olten/Switzerland

Contact E-mail Address:
th_greuter@bluewin.ch

Introduction: Swallowed topical corticosteroids are highly efficacious in inducing clinical and histological remission in patients with active eosinophilic oesophagitis (EoE) and also in maintaining such remission. However, it has not yet been evaluated if a long-lasting remission can be achieved, and whether maintenance treatment can be stopped once patients have achieved such a remission.
Aims & Methods: Since 2007, adult and adolescent EoE patients included into a large cohort at the Swiss EoE Clinics were treated long-term with swallowed topical corticosteroids. Clinical, endoscopic and histological disease activity was assessed at annual visits. In patients that achieved clinical (no EoE-related symptoms), endoscopic (absence of white exudates, furrows, and edema) and histological remission (peak eosinophilic count <5/hpf) for at least 6 months (defined as deep remission), treatment was stopped. All patients treated at the Swiss EoE Clinics according to this concept were analyzed retrospectively.
Results: Thirty-three of the 370 patients (8.9%) who were treated with swallowed topical corticosteroids achieved deep remission. Mean age of remitters at disease onset was 35.7 years (±17.4) and median diagnostic delay was 5.4 years (IQR 1.2–11.4). Median time to clinical, endoscopic and histological remission was 26.0 weeks (IQR 4.3–77.0), 72.5 weeks (IQR 58.6–104.1) and 61.4 weeks (IQR 14.3–101.3), respectively. Deep remission was achieved after a median of 82.9 weeks (IQR 64.4–172.3). The proportion of female patients was higher in the group of patients that achieved remission when compared to those that did not (19/33, 57.6% vs. 79/337, 23.4%, p = 0.016). No differences with regards to the age at disease onset, diagnostic delay, family history of EoE, concomitant atopic diseases and serum IgE levels between remitters and non-remitters were observed. Female sex was an independent prognostic factor for achieving deep remission (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.17–5.13, p = 0.017). Overall, swallowed topical corticosteroids were stopped after 104.7 weeks (IQR 65.5–176.6). A cumulative dose of 297.5 mg (IQR 216.0–529.9) was required. Only two patients were concomitantly treated with PPI. No mucosal damage, such as epithelial atrophy or dysplasia, was observed upon histologic examination. In 27 of the 33 remitters (81.8%) a clinical relapse occurred after a median of 26.0 weeks (95% CI 6.7–45.3) after treatment cessation. Six remitters (18.2%) did not experience a clinical relapse during a median follow-up of 35.5 weeks (IQR 18.4–45.4) after cessation of swallowed topical corticosteroids.
Conclusion: Only a minority of EoE patients achieved deep remission despite adequate long-term treatment with topical corticosteroids. Female sex is the only prognostic factor for achievement of deep remission. After cessation of the medication the majority of patients experienced a relapse.
Disclosure of Interest: All authors have declared no conflicts of interest.

J. Colombel1, G. D'Haens2, W. Reinisch3, E.V. Loftus Jr4, R. Panaccione5, J. Satsangi6, G. Alperovich7, S. Berg8, J. Kalabic9, M. Bereswill10, J. Petersson11, A.M. Robinson12

Introduction: The global post-marketing observational registry PYRAMID assessed the long-term safety and effectiveness of adalimumab (ADA) as used in routine clinical practice in patients with moderately to severely active Crohn’s disease (CD).
Aims & Methods: Patients were enrolled in the registry if they were newly prescribed ADA or currently receiving ADA according to the local product label; patients were followed for up to 6 years. This analysis assessed the long-term safety of ADA by age subgroups (<40, 40–59, and ≥60 years) at registry enrolment (baseline). Registry treatment-emergent (TE) adverse events (AEs), defined as any event with onset on/after first dose of ADA in the registry up to 70 days after last ADA injection are reported as events per 100 patient-years (PY).
Results: A total of 5025 patients in the registry received at least one dose of ADA and were included in the analysis; at baseline, 2981 patients (59.3%) were aged <40 years (female, 57.1%; median age, 29.0 years; median CD duration, 7.0 years), 1717 patients (34.2%) were aged 40–59 years (female, 57.8%; median age, 47.0 years; median CD duration, 13.0 years) and 327 patients (6.5%) were aged ≥60 years (female, 52.9%; median age, 64.0 years; median CD duration, 13.5 years). Of those aged ≥60 years at baseline, 23/327 (7.0%) were ≥75 years old. Cumulative registry ADA exposure by baseline age groups was 9681.1 PY (<40 years), 6009.3 PY (40– 59 years) and 990.0 PY (≥60 years). Approximately 46–52% of patients were receiving ADA monotherapy (without immunomodulators or corticosteroids) at baseline across the age subgroups. Rates of any registry TEAEs, including serious AEs and AEs of special interest, by age subgroups at baseline are shown in Table 1. Similar rates of registry TE serious infections and opportunistic infections were observed across the younger age subgroups, but numerically higher in the ≥60 years subgroup. Rates of any registry TE malignancies and non-melanoma skin cancer were significantly higher in older patients (aged ≥60 years at baseline). There was no event of lymphoma reported in the subgroup of patients aged ≥60 years at baseline; however, during the follow-up in the registry, 3 patients classified in the 40–59 years at baseline age group were diagnosed with lymphoma when they were ≥60 years of age. No patients in the ≥60 years group reported active/latent tuberculosis.

 Conclusion: Long-term treatment with ADA was well tolerated in patients with moderately to severely active CD, irrespective of patient age. The rate of exposure-adjusted registry TEAEs (per 100 PY) was generally higher in older (≥60 years) compared to younger patients (<60 years); however, no new safety signals were identified in this age group.

## OP351 EXPOSURE TO COMBINATION THERAPY WITH THIOPURINES AND ANTI-TNF AGENTS IS ASSOCIATED WITH REDUCED INCIDENCE OF ACUTE ARTERIAL EVENTS IN PATIENTS WITH INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE (IBD): A NATIONWIDE FRENCH COHORT STUDY
J. Kirchgesner1, N.N. Andersen2, F. Carrat3, M. Schwarzinger4, T. Jess5, L. Beaugerie6

1UMRS 1136, INSERM, UPMC Univ Paris 06Sorbonne Universités, Paris/France

2Department Of Epidemiology Research, Statens Serum Institute, Copenhagen/Denmark

3Department Of Public Health, AP-HP, Hôpital Saint-Antoine, Paris/France

4Then, Translational Health Economics Network, Paris/France

5Department Of Clinical Epidemiology, Bispebjerg Hospital, Copenhagen/Denmark

6Department Of Gastroenterology, AP-HP, Hôpital Saint-Antoine, Paris/France

Contact E-mail Address:
julien.kirchgesner@gmx.com

Introduction: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at increased risk of acute arterial events, probably due to a systemic inflammation leading to atherosclerosis. Anti-TNFs and thiopurines are effective in the treatment of patients with IBD and may, due to their anti-inflammatory properties, lower the risk of acute arterial events, however this remains unknown.
Aims & Methods: The aim of this study was to assess the impact of thiopurines and anti-TNFs on risk of acute arterial events in patients with IBD. Patients affiliated to the French national health insurance with a diagnosis of IBD based on listed long-term diseases (30 chronic diseases, including IBD, that allow for a 100% reimbursement of health expenses) and/or hospital discharge diagnosis were included from 2010 to 2012, and followed up until 31 December 2014. Occurrence of acute arterial events, cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes, obesity, smoking, and alcohol use disorder), surgical procedures, and hospitalisations related to IBD was assessed. Acute arterial events included ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, and peripheral artery disease excluding acute mesenteric ischemia. Risks of acute arterial events were compared between thiopurines and anti-TNFs exposed and unexposed patients with marginal structural Cox proportional hazard models adjusting for baseline and time-varying demographics, medications, and comorbidities, including IBD disease activity.
Results: A total of 178,360 IBD patients were included (54% females, mean age at cohort entry 46.3 years, 50.7% Crohn’s disease). Among them, 22.8%, 13.5% and 5.7% were exposed to thiopurine monotherapy, anti-TNF monotherapy and combination therapy during follow-up, respectively. Overall, 4376 incident acute arterial events occurred (incidence rates: 5.6 per 1000 PY, person-years), including 2204 (50.4%) ischemic heart diseases, 1476 (33.7%) cerebrovascular diseases, and 696 (15.9%) peripheral artery diseases. Exposure to thiopurine monotherapy, anti-TNF monotherapy and combination therapy were all numerically associated with a decreased risk of acute arterial events compared to unexposed patients, but the difference was only statistically significant for patients exposed to combination therapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0.91; confidence interval 95% [0.82–1.02], HR95%: 0.90 [0.77–1.04], HR95%: 0.82 [0.68–0.99], respectively). Similar findings were found for ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease and peripheral artery disease. The magnitude in risk reduction was highest in men with Crohn’s disease exposed to combination therapy (HR 95%: 0.61 [0.44–0.85]).
Conclusion: Exposure to combination therapy with thiopurines and anti-TNFs is associated with decreased risk of acute arterial events in patients with IBD, particularly in men with Crohn’s disease. Prevention of acute arterial events should be considered in the benefit-risk balance assessment of thiopurines and anti-TNFs treatment in patients with IBD.

## OP352 PYRAMID REGISTRY: LONG-TERM SAFETY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF ADALIMUMAB BY BASELINE IMMUNOMODULATOR USE IN PATIENTS WITH CROHN’S DISEASE
W. Reinisch1, R. Panaccione2, G. R. D'Haens3, E.V. Loftus Jr4, J. Satsangi5, J. Colombel6, G. Alperovich7, S. Berg8, J. Kalabic9, M. Bereswill10, J. Petersson11, A.M. Robinson12

Effectiveness was measured using the Harvey Bradshaw index (HBI) and was calculated for all pts who received ≥1 dose of ADA in the registry and summarised for pts with available data at the respective registry visits (as observed analysis). Remission (HBI < 5) was assessed at each visit in ADA mono and combo groups. Rates of registry treatment-emergent (TE) adverse events (AEs), defined as any event with onset on/after first dose of ADA in the registry up to 70 days after last ADA injection, are reported as events (E)/100 patient-years (PY).
Results: At BL, 3227/5025 pts (64.2%) were receiving ADA mono (58.1% female; median age, 36.0 years; median CD duration, 8.4 years) and 1798/5025 pts (35.8%) were receiving ADA + IMM (55.3% female; median age, 35.0 years; median CD duration, 8.8 years). The mean ± SD duration of ADA exposure during the registry was similar for pts receiving ADA mono (1179.6 ± 837.8 days) and combo therapy (1271.4 ± 828.0 days). One year after enrolment, a similarly high proportion of pts (approximately 70%) in the ADA mono and combo groups achieved remission. Rates of remission were sustained over time during PYRAMID and were similar between the subgroups. Similar rates of registry TEAEs (37.4 E/100 PY vs 35.6E/100 PY), serious AEs (25.1 E/100 PY vs 24.1 E/100 PY), serious infections (4.7 E/100 PY vs 4.8 E/100 PY), and AEs leading to treatment discontinuation (4.7E/100 PY vs 4.4 E/100 PY) were reported for pts receiving ADA mono and combo therapy, respectively. Numerically higher proportion of pts with ≥1 event of any AE, serious infections, AEs leading to discontinuation, and significantly more pts with ≥1 serious AEs (39.5% [95%CI 37.3–41.8] vs 35.4%, [95%CI 33.7–37.1]) were seen for combo vs mono therapy. Malignancy rates were 0.7 E/100 PY (n[%] = 62[1.9]) in the ADA mono group and 1.0 E/100 PY (n[%] = 54[3.0]) in the combo group, with a significant difference in non-melanoma skin cancer incidence rates (0.2 [95%CI, 0.10–0.27] E/100 PY (n[%] = 12[0.4]) vs (0.5 [95%CI, 0.34–0.70] E/100 PY (n[%] = 24[1.3])), but similar rates for lymphoma (<0.1 E/100 PY (n[%] = 5[0.2]) vs (<0.1 E/100 PY (n[%] = 5[0.2]).

 Conclusion: The long-term effectiveness of ADA in pts with moderately to severely active CD enrolled in the PYRAMID registry was similar for those treated with ADA mono or combo therapy at registry entry. Exposure-adjusted malignancy rates tended to be higher in pts treated with ADA combo therapy.

## OP353 INTEGRATED SAFETY ANALYSES OF TOFACITINIB IN ULCERATIVE COLITIS CLINICAL TRIALS
W. J. Sandborn1, J. Panés2, G. D’Haens3, B. E. Sands4, C. Su5, M. Moscariello5, T.V. Jones5, R. Pedersen5, G. Friedman5, N. Lawendy5, G. Chan5

1Division Of Gastroenterology, University of California, La Jolla, San Diego/United States of America/CA

2Hospital Clinic de Barcelona, IDIBAPS, CIBERehd, Barcelona/Spain

3Department Of Gastroenterology, Academic Medical Centre, Amsterdam/Netherlands

4Dr. Henry D. Janowitz Division Of Gastroenterology, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York/United States of America/NY

5Pfizer Inc, Collegeville/United States of America/PA

Contact E-mail Address:
wsandborn@ucsd.edu

Introduction: Tofacitinib is an oral, small molecule Janus kinase inhibitor that is being investigated for ulcerative colitis (UC). The efficacy and safety of tofacitinib for treatment of moderate to severe UC was evaluated in induction and maintenance Phase (P) 3, randomised, placebo (PBO)-controlled studies.1, 2
Aims & Methods: We describe safety data for tofacitinib in patients (pts) with moderate to severe UC, based on integrated analyses of one P2 (8 weeks) and two P3 induction (8 weeks each) studies, one P3 maintenance (52 weeks) study and one long-term extension (LTE) study (ongoing). Analyses were performed for three cohorts (C): C1, P2P3 induction studies; C2, P3 maintenance study; and C3, tofacitinib-treated pts in P2P3 LTE studies. Pts received tofacitinib 10 mg twice daily (BID) in P3 induction studies and 5 and 10 mg BID in P3 maintenance and open-label LTE studies. Adverse events (AEs) of special interest (opportunistic infections [OIs], malignancies, major adverse cardiovascular events [MACEs], hepatic injury and gastrointestinal perforation [GIP]) were reviewed by independent adjudication committees.
Results: Of 1240 pts, 1156 received ≥1 dose of tofacitinib 5 or 10 mg BID with 1366 patient-years (PY) of tofacitinib exposure and up to 3.9 years of treatment. 85% of pts primarily received tofacitinib 10 mg BID. Demographics and baseline characteristics were similar across treatment arms within each cohort. There were a total of 4 deaths in C3. The proportion of pts with AEs, serious AEs (SAEs) and severe AEs was similar between treatment arms within C1 and C2. In C3, the most common AEs were nasopharyngitis and worsening of UC. Serious infections occurred in ≤1% of pts in any treatment arm in C1 and C2, with similar incidence rates (IRs) between arms in C2. Herpes zoster (HZ) IRs for tofacitinib 5 (2.05/100 PY), or 10 mg BID (6.64/100 PY) in C2 were numerically higher than PBO (0.97/100 PY). In C3, most HZ were limited to cutaneous involvement and non-SAEs. OIs were infrequent, and mainly HZ (14/18 events). Tofacitinib arms in C2 had no malignancies (excl. non-melanoma skin cancer [NMSC]), or GIP, and both NMSC and MACE IRs were similar to PBO. IRs of serious infection, OI, HZ, NMSC and MACE in C3 were generally similar to those in C2. In C3, there were no Hy’s law cases; GIP occurred in 3 pts and malignancies (excl. NMSC) occurred in 7 pts without specific cancer type clustering.

 Conclusion: The tofacitinib UC programme provided a robust safety database, and integrated analyses revealed no unexpected safety signals. These results showed an overall acceptable safety profile for tofacitinib 10 mg BID induction therapy and for tofacitinib 5 and 10 mg BID maintenance therapy in pts with moderate to severe UC.

## OP354 LONG-TERM HEALTH OUTCOMES OF 1000 CHILDREN BORN TO MOTHERS WITH INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE IN THE ANTI-TNF ERA
S. Kanis1, S. Modderman2, J.C. Escher3, R. Beukers4, K.h.n. De Boer5, A. Bodelier6, A. Depla7, G. Dijkstra8, A. Van Dijk1, L. P. l. Gilissen9, F. Hoentjen10, J.M. Jansen11, J. Kuijvenhoven12, N. Introduction: Long-term health outcomes of children born to mothers with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) are relatively unexplored. The aim of this study was to describe the long-term health of children born to mothers with IBD and to assess whether medication use affects outcome.
Aims & Methods: We performed a multicenter retrospective study in The Netherlands. Women diagnosed with IBD prior to their pregnancy giving birth from January 1999 through April 2015 were identified in 20 participating hospitals and were invited per letter to participate. After consent, information regarding disease characteristics, medication use, life style factors during pregnancy (smoking, folic acid intake), birth outcomes (gestational age, birth weight, major congenital abnormalities) and long-term health outcomes of children (growth, severe infections necessitating hospitalization, chronic diseases and adverse reactions to vaccinations) were retrieved during a telephone interview with the mother. Information regarding antibiotic-treated infections was retrieved from the general practitioners (GPs). Adverse long-term health outcomes were defined as growth failure for which children were referred to a pediatrician, hospital admission because of a severe infection and/or chronic disease.
Results: From 20 Dutch hospitals, 1000 children born to 605 mothers (369 (61%) Crohn’s Disease (CD), 217 (36%) ulcerative colitis (UC), 19 (3%) IBDU) were included. Median follow up was 60 (IQR 36–60) months. In utero, 198 (20%) children had been exposed to anti-TNF, 241 (24%) to thiopurine monotherapy, 80 (1%) to systemic steroids and 481 (48%) to 5-ASA or no IBD medication. During pregnancy, mothers diagnosed with UC/IBDU more often relapsed (n = 138, 36%) than mothers with CD (n = 92, 15%) (p = 0.0001) and an endoscopy during pregnancy was more often performed in women with UC/IBDU (n = 49, 13%) than women with CD (n = 30, 5%) (p = 0.0001). Anti-TNF treatment was more often stopped before the third trimester (n = 87, 55%) in CD women than UC/IBDU women (n = 11, 28%) (p = 0.002). However, birth outcomes were similar for both groups. Exposure to anti-TNF and/or thiopurine was not associated with adverse birth outcomes, however, after adjusting for disease activity, systemic steroids use was associated with preterm birth (aOR 2.67, 95%CI 1.59–4.47). A total of 143 adverse health outcomes were reported in 132 children; 111 (11%) children were admitted to hospital for a severe infection of which, 74 (69%) occurred in the first year of life; 16 (2%) had growth failure and 16 (2%) children were diagnosed with a chronic disease before the age of 5 years. Seven children (1%) were treated for an adverse reaction to vaccination. Information from the GPs was retrieved for 668 (67%) children showing a median number of antibiotic-treated infections per year of 0.3 (IQR 0.00- 0.68). The number of children treated for one or more infections were the highest in year 1 (n = 240, 38%) and year 2 (n = 218, 38%). This infection rate decreased significantly over time to 104 (26%) children in year 5 (p = 0.0001). IBD type and IBD treatment did not influence long-term adverse health outcomes, adverse reaction to vaccination or infection rates.
Conclusion: In our long-term follow-up study, we found no evidence that IBD type or medical treatment for IBD during pregnancy affects long-term health outcomes of children. On behalf of the Initiative on Crohn and Colitis (ICC).

## OP355 SAFETY OF HERPES ZOSTER VACCINATION AMONG INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE PATIENTS BEING TREATED WITH ANTI-TNF MEDICATIONS
C. Trivedi1, Y. Shah2, N. Khan2

1Gastroenterology, Corporal Michael J. Crescenz VAMC, Philadelphia/United States of America/PA

2Gastroenterology, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia/United States of America/PA

Contact E-mail Address:
nabeel.khan@va.gov

Introduction: The risk of herpes zoster (HZ) is elevated in patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) who are treated with anti-TNF medications. However, since herpes zoster vaccine (HZV) is a live vaccine, it is not recommended to be administered in patients who are currently taking anti-TNF medications. ECCO suggests administering HZV 3 weeks prior to starting the immunosuppressive therapy or 3–6 months after stopping it. Although it is optimal to give the HZV prior to starting anti-TNF medications, in many clinical scenarios there is an urgent need to start the medication.
Aims & Methods: Our aim was to determine the safety of giving HZV while patients are on anti-TNF therapy. We conducted a retrospective cohort study involving IBD patients who were followed in the Veterans Affairs (VA) healthcare system between 2001 and 2016. We obtained inpatient and outpatient pharmacy data on our patients from the VA’s Pharmacy Benefits Management database and exposure periods to infliximab, adalimumab, certolizumab and golimumab were determined. Patients who received HZV while on anti-TNF medication were identified through vaccination codes and confirmed through individual chart review. Our outcome of interest was development of herpes zoster (HZ) between 0–42 days post HZV administration. This was determined by individual review of the patients’ charts.

 Results: 56,417 patients with IBD were followed in the VA healthcare system from 2001 to 2016. A total of 59 patients were on an anti-TNF medication when they were given the HZV, and amongst them, 13 (22%) were also taking a thiopurine. Majority of the population was male and caucasian i.e. 51 (86.4%) and 53 (89.8%) respectively. Almost all patients 56 (94.9%) had charlson comorbidity index (CCI) of ≥2 (Table 1). The median interval between the start of anti-TNF therapy and HZV was 88 days (IQR 29–481.5). Median duration between the last administration of infliximab and administration of HZV was 23 days (IQR 13.5–32.25) while for adalimumab, median was 8 days (IQR 4.75–10.25). Median age of at the time of HZV was 64.9 years (IQR 60–69). Median number of encounters within 42 days after receiving HZV was 2 (IQR 2–3). No case of HZ related to live zoster vaccine type virus was found within 0–42 days of HZV administration.
Conclusion: In this nationwide cohort of patients, our data suggest that administering the HZV to IBD patients who are concomitantly taking anti-TNF medications is relatively safe. This study significantly expands the evidence supporting the use of HZV in this population, having included an elderly group of patients with a high CCI who are likely at a much higher risk of developing HZ.

All other authors have declared no conflicts of interest.
